facts.text: Barstow was founded in 1902 as a stop on the Washington and Great Northern Railway, named after the contractor who supervised the line.
A 1947 prefabricated steel Pratt truss bridge over the Kettle River, built from surplus WWII materials, now sits about a mile southeast of the original 1906 wagon bridge.
Barstow’s early economy relied on logging, lumbering, and intermittent marble quarrying, but the rugged terrain limited large‑scale agriculture.
The community remains sparsely populated, with most of its 52 housing units occupied and a median household income above the county average.
Barstow lies along U.S. Route 395, 14 miles north of Kettle Falls and 17 miles south of the Canadian border.
